In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic treatment with DA receptor antagonists and DA agonists can affect the biosynthesis and the proteolytic conversion of β-endorphins in a region-specific and hormone-specific manner.

chronic treatment with DA receptor ligands induces changes in the activity and/or number of cells producing β-endorphin, and that these changes are accompanied by parallel changes in the processing of β -endo-phin to γ-endorphin in pitui- tary and brain, and to α-endorphin only in the pituitary.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing of β -endorphin in the intermediate lobo is not affected by chronic DA receptor blockade, whereas the biosynthetic activity is stimulated.

the processing of β -endophrin in the intermediate lobo is regulated independently from that of the anterior lobe and that the proteolytic cleavage of β -endorphine is regulated differently in different areas of the brain.

the effects of chronic haloperidol or bromocriptin treatment on the levels of immunoreactivity and the ratios of the different endorphins in the pituitary and in the brain are not only dependent on the effects of the drugs on the DA receptor but also depend on other factors such as the site of action of the drug and the type of cells involved in the biosynthesis and proteolytic processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteolytic conversion of the precursor, β-endorphin into α- and γ-endorphin is not a fixed ratio but is subject to modulation.
the processing of the precursor molecule β-endorphin can be affected by chronic treatment with DA receptor ligands.

the processing of β -endophrin can be modulated by chronic treatment with DA receptor ligands, which suggests that the proteolytic enzymes involved in the processing of β-endophrin may be modulated by DA receptors.
